newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway to free Bosnian hijacker early amid protest.
newsitem.headline: Norway to free Bosnian hijacker early amid protest.

text.p: A Bosnian Moslem serving a four-year prison term for hijacking a Norwegian plane will be released soon, after completing little more than half of his sentence, Norwegian authorities said on Thursday.

The decision to free Haris Kec early was sharply criticised by the Norwegian Pilots' Association, which said the mild sentence and the early release sent a signal to would-be hijackers that Norway was a haven for air pirates.
"He applied for an early release and was granted it," said Erik Lund-Isaksen, head of the prisoners' rehabilitation section of the justice ministry. "I won't say why."
Lund-Isaken said Kec, who would have been eligible for parole in March next year, would probably be free by Christmas to return to Sarajevo, his home town.
Kec commandeered a domestic Scandinavian Airlines System plane with 116 passengers and six crew in November 1994 after takeoff from Bardufoss inside the Arctic circle.
Claiming he had bombs and hand grenades, he had threatened to set them off unless Norway took the lead in an international effort to bring food and other necessities to war-torn Bosnia.
He surrendered at Oslo's Gardermoen airport after an eight-hour drama in which nobody was injured and it turned out he had no weapons of any kind.
The Oslo City Court handed down the relatively mild verdict in June 1995 citing mitigating circumstances. Hijacking in Norway carries a sentence of between two and 21 years in prison.

Kjell Erik Heibek of the pilots' association said: "First of all he is being released much earlier than ordinary criminals in this country. Secondly, the sentence was low compared to the very serious criminal act that a hijacking is.

"No crew can ever treat a hijacking as if it were harmless. We can't assume that a hijacker is not carrying bombs or grenades. As long as he says he is armed we have to act as if he were armed," Heibek said.
Kec came to Norway from Bosnia in 1993 and was allowed to stay on humanitarian grounds.
